concerns: Comparative claims were detected without a suitable baseline in the available text.
The evaluation is conducted in a production-like harness rather than a fully deployed production system, so real-world deployment benefits remain to be demonstrated.

Some subgroup effects (e.g., probing advantage varying by world or model) have overlapping confidence intervals, and the authors appropriately treat these as mechanism interpretations rather than resolved effects.
The paper does not report statistical significance tests beyond confidence intervals, which limits the strength of some comparative claims.
Code and data availability are not explicitly stated in the extracted text, which limits independent replication.
The selected case studies in the appendices are acknowledged as not establishing the aggregate effect, though they are illustrative.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The paper introduces environment-probing curation, a deployment-compatible extension that gives a post-task curator agent read-only world tools to verify, scope, and refresh candidate memories before writing. The authors diagnose the retrospective evidence boundary of trajectory-only curation and propose a propose-probe-commit process. Evaluation on CLBench and adapted APEX shows improved pass rates, reward, and cost efficiency across multiple models, with detailed qualitative evidence and explicit limitations.

positive_signals: The available text identifies data or a benchmark used by the work.
The work reports an error or qualitative analysis.
Formal definitions or proof-oriented evidence is present.
Dataset documentation, quality control, licensing, or ethics is discussed.

Clear diagnosis of the retrospective evidence boundary in post-task memory curation, with concrete failure modes (memorized instance answers, inherited inefficient paths, unverifiable scope, blind spots, staleness).
Deployment-compatible design that requires no retraining and leaves the task agent, retriever, memory representation, and production write authority unchanged.
Substantial evaluation across two benchmarks (CLBench and adapted APEX), four system configurations, and three model families (GPT-5.4, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7).
Cost-aware metrics (pass-discounted reward, task-agent cost, reward gain per dollar) that go beyond accuracy alone.
Detailed appendices with prompts, runtime architecture, benchmark construction, and side-by-side trajectory evidence.
Explicit acknowledgment of limitations, including overlapping confidence intervals and the selected nature of case studies.
Qualitative analysis of memory records showing the shift from answer-anchored warnings to executable procedures.
